race_context: The Duneland School Corporation serves more than 5,800 students in Westchester, Jackson and Liberty townships and part of Pine Township in Porter County. Its 92-square-mile area includes Chesterton, Porter, Burns Harbor and Dune Acres {dsc_welcome}. It runs five K–4 elementary schools, two intermediate schools (grades 5–6), two middle schools (grades 7–8) and Chesterton High School {dsc_welcome}. Chesterton Middle School closed in 2024 {wiki_dsc}.

Superintendent: Dr. Chip Pettit, superintendent since 2019, left at the end of the 2025–26 school year; the district announced his departure on January 29, 2026 {dsc_soty}{dsc_news}. The district now lists Robert McDermott as superintendent and Dr. Benjamin Tonagel as assistant superintendent {dsc_admin}. On March 12, 2026 the board held the required public hearing on a three-year superintendent contract running July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029, with a base salary of $210,000 {dsc_contract}.

The board has five elected members {dsc_welcome}. The current members are President Brandon Kroft, Vice President Alayna Lightfoot Pol, Secretary Beth Mehling, Jocelyn Hibshman and Kirk Redman {dsc_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot (per the state list): At Large, Liberty Township, and Westchester/Pine Township, one member each {in_list}. All three candidates who are current board members are running: Lightfoot Pol (At Large), Mehling (Liberty Township) and Kroft (Westchester/Pine) {in_list}{dsc_board}. Lightfoot Pol and Mehling won Duneland board seats in 2022 {lpm_2022}. The At Large and Liberty Township races are uncontested. In Westchester/Pine, Kroft faces Mitchell J. (Mitch) Reynolds, who is not a board member {in_list}{dsc_board}.
Not on this ballot: Hibshman and Redman {in_list}{dsc_board}.

Operating referendum (2025): on June 26, 2025 the board adopted a resolution to ask voters on November 4, 2025 for an eight-year operating levy of up to 39 cents per $100 of assessed value and up to $16,179,502 a year, citing 'reductions in property tax revenue.' The state approved the ballot language on July 16, 2025 {dlgf_dsc_det}{dlgf_dsc_plan}. The state's ballot-language findings put the increase at $707 a year on a $350,000 median home {dlgf_dsc_det}. The district's spending plan splits the money four ways: $8.1 million a year to maintain class sizes, $3.3 million to attract and retain teachers and staff, $2.4 million for academic programs and $2.38 million for student health and safety {dlgf_dsc_plan}. Earlier Duneland referendums passed in May 2012 and May 2019 {dlgf_hist}{dlgf_dsc_det}. This guide could not confirm the November 2025 result from an official source. The district's 2027 budget notice lists a current-year referendum-fund levy of $16,179,151, close to the requested maximum {dsc_form3}.

Budget (2026–2027): the district's notice for the 2027 budget proposes a 2027 budget of $98.95 million: Education $46.7 million, Operations $24 million, Debt Service $15.25 million and Referendum $13 million {dsc_form3}. The notice estimates the district's property-tax cap credit (revenue lost to the caps) at $2,279,400 {dsc_form3}. The budget hearing was set for October 12, 2026, with adoption on October 26, 2026 {dsc_form3}{dsc_meetings}.

Facilities: from 2022 to December 2024 the district built a new Yost Elementary School and renovated four other elementary schools and both intermediate/middle schools. It followed with 2025 projects including playground replacements, soccer stadium renovations and carpet replacement at Chesterton High School {dsc_capital}.
Other 2026 items: a phone-free policy took effect July 1, 2026 {dsc_home}.

Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news coverage of the 2026 Duneland races. The district's BoardDocs agendas and minutes could not be opened, so individual board votes could not be reviewed {dsc_meetings}.
